deathBeat: d19: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Deirdre McKenna is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d19: 🕯️ Deirdre McKenna is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d19: The village's quarrel was with Deirdre — and Deirdre is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d20: That night, they bring Deirdre home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d19: At the grave, Glody speaks for Fiona — "Deirdre trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d19: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d19: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d20: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
d20: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 1,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.

d20: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.

d22: You say a few words for Deirdre. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d22: You bury Deirdre. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
d23: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+2 integration)
echoSample: d22: "Good question." "Deirdre owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d22: "Deirdre always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d26: "Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Deirdre is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
d26: "Nobody says Deirdre's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
d26: "Since Deirdre died... I keep expecting to see Deirdre at the fire. Stupid."
d26: "I keep turning over the last thing Deirdre said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
